title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Say how you feel, give your opinion, agree and disagree, and link ideas with 'because', 'but' and 'so'.
intro:
Sindhi is a language of feeling — its great poet Shah Abdul Latif wrote almost entirely about longing, love and separation. In everyday speech, many emotions use the same **کي** pattern you already know: **مون کي ڊپ ٿو لڳي** 'fear strikes me' = I'm scared, **مون کي تنهنجي ياد اچي ٿي** 'your memory comes to me' = I miss you.

You'll also learn to say 'I think that…' and to join sentences with **ڇاڪاڻ ته** 'because', **پر** 'but' and **تنهن ڪري** 'so'.

grammar.title: Opinions: 'I think that…', agreeing and disagreeing
grammar.body:
Sindhi joins a thought to its content with **ته** (ta) 'that':

**مان سمجهان ٿو ته …** — I think / believe that … (lit. I understand that)
**مون کي لڳي ٿو ته …** — it seems to me that …, I feel that …
**منهنجي خيال ۾ …** — in my opinion …
**منهنجو خيال آهي ته …** — my view is that …

The clause after ته is a normal sentence with the verb at the end.

**Agreeing**: ها، صحيح آهي · بلڪل · توهان صحيح آهيو · مان توهان سان متفق آهيان · مان مڃان ٿو.
**Disagreeing (politely)**: معاف ڪجو، پر … · مان متفق ناهيان · منهنجو خيال ٻيو آهي 'I see it differently' · اهو ٺيڪ ناهي.

Ask for someone's view with **توهان جو ڇا خيال آهي؟** 'What's your opinion?'

examples.roman: māṃ samujhāṃ tho ta sindhī sikhaṇu āsānu āhe.
examples.en: I think learning Sindhi is easy. (man)

examples.en: Sorry, but I see it differently.

examples.roman: māṃ tavhāṃ sāṃ sau saikiṛo mutafiqu āhiyāṃ.
examples.en: I agree with you one hundred percent.

grammar.title: Joining ideas: ۽، پر، يا، ڇاڪاڻ ته، تنهن ڪري
grammar.body:
The main conjunctions:

**۽** ai — and (written with the special sign ۽)
**يا** yā — or
**پر** para — but
**ڇاڪاڻ ته** chhākāṇa ta — because (also ڇو ته chho ta)
**تنهن ڪري** tanhin kare / **ان ڪري** un kare — so, therefore
**جيتوڻيڪ** jetoṇīka — although

They go at the start of the clause they introduce, just like in English: مان ٿڪل آهيان، **تنهن ڪري** گهر ٿو وڃان 'I'm tired, so I'm going home'.

Feelings with کي: **مون کي ڪاوڙ آئي** 'anger came to me' (= I got angry), **مون کي ڊپ ٿو لڳي** 'I'm scared', **مون کي … جي ياد اچي ٿي** 'I miss …', **مون کي … جو شوق آهي** 'I'm keen on …'.

examples.native: مان خوش آهيان ڇاڪاڻ ته اڄ موڪل آهي.
examples.roman: māṃ xushu āhiyāṃ chhākāṇa ta aʄu mokala āhe.
examples.en: I'm happy because today is a holiday.

examples.native: فلم ڊگهي هئي، پر دلچسپ هئي.
examples.roman: filma ḍighī huī, para dilchaspu huī.
examples.en: The film was long, but interesting.

examples.native: مينهن پيو وسي، تنهن ڪري اسين گهر ۾ آهيون.
examples.roman: mīṃhu peyo vase, tanhin kare asīṃ ghara meṃ āhyūṃ.
examples.en: It's raining, so we're at home.
Will you have tea or coffee?

examples.native: جيتوڻيڪ هو ٿڪل هو، پر ڪم ڪندو رهيو.
examples.roman: jetoṇīka hū thakalu ho, para kamu kando rahyo.
examples.en: Although he was tired, he kept working.

dialogue.title: After the concert
dialogue.setting: Sorath and John walk out of a Sufi music evening in Bhit Shah.

lines.speaker: Sorath
lines.native: ڪيئن لڳو؟ توهان جو ڇا خيال آهي؟
lines.roman: kīeṃ laɠo? tavhāṃ jo chhā xiyālu āhe?
lines.en: How was it? What do you think?

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: ڏاڍو سٺو! مان حيران آهيان. مون لفظ نه سمجهيا، پر دل کي ڇهي ويو.
lines.roman: ɗāḍho suṭho! māṃ hairānu āhiyāṃ. moṃ lafza na samujhyā, para dila khe chhuhī vayo.
lines.en: Wonderful! I'm amazed. I didn't understand the words, but it touched my heart.

lines.speaker: Sorath
lines.native: اهو ئي ته شاهه جو ڪمال آهي.
lines.roman: uho ī ta shāh jo kamālu āhe.
lines.en: That's exactly the magic of Shah Latif.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: ڳائڻ وارا اداس ڇو لڳي رهيا هئا؟
lines.roman: ɠāiṇa vārā udāsu chho laɠī rahyā huā?
lines.en: Why did the singers seem sad?

lines.speaker: Sorath
lines.native: ڇاڪاڻ ته هي بيت سسئيءَ جي ڏک بابت آهن. هوءَ پنهونءَ کي پئي ڳولي.
lines.roman: chhākāṇa ta hī beta sasuīa je ɗukha bābata āhin. hūa panhūa khe paī ɠole.
lines.en: Because these verses are about Sassui's sorrow. She is searching for Punhun.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: مان سمجهان ٿو ته هي دنيا جي سڀ کان سهڻي موسيقي آهي.
lines.roman: māṃ samujhāṃ tho ta hī dunyā jī sabha khāṃ sohaṇī mausīqī āhe.
lines.en: I think this is the most beautiful music in the world.

lines.speaker: Sorath
lines.native: مان متفق آهيان! پر مان سنڌي آهيان، تنهن ڪري منهنجي راءِ ۾ ٿورو تعصب آهي.
lines.roman: māṃ mutafiqu āhiyāṃ! para māṃ sindhī āhiyāṃ, tanhin kare munhinjī rāi meṃ thoro taʿasubu āhe.
lines.en: I agree! But I'm Sindhi, so I'm a little biased.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: ها ها! ايندڙ سال وري اچڻ جي اميد آهي.
lines.roman: hā hā! endaṛa sāla varī achaṇa jī umīda āhe.
lines.en: Ha ha! I hope to come again next year.

culture: **Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai** (1689–1752), Sindh's greatest poet, is revered by Sindhis of every faith. His collected verse, **Shah jo Risalo** (شاهه جو رسالو), retells folk tales — Sassui and Punhun, Umar and Marvi, Sohni and Mehar, Noori and Jam Tamachi, Moomal and Rano, Leela and Chanesar — as Sufi allegories of the soul's longing for the Divine. Every evening at his shrine in **Bhit Shah**, the faqirs sing his verses in the traditional *vāī* style to the **tambooro** (تنبورو), and his annual ʿurs draws huge crowds. Quoting a line of Shah Latif is the surest way to a Sindhi's heart.

tip.title: I'm tired, she's worried
tip.body:
- Feelings use آهي like any description: مان ٿڪل **آهيان**، هوءَ پريشان **آهي**.
- Most feeling words never change: اداس، ٿڪل، پريشان، حيران.
- But 'very' agrees with the person: a man is **ڏاڍو** خوش, a woman **ڏاڍي** خوش, a group **ڏاڍا** خوش.
- Ask why: تون اداس **ڇو** آهين؟

sentences.roman: māṃ pareshānu nāhiyāṃ, raɠo thakalu āhiyāṃ.

lessons.title: Scared, angry, missing someone

tip.title: Feelings that "come to" you: کي
tip.body:
- Many feelings happen *to* you, so the person takes **کي**: مون کي **ڊپ ٿو لڳي** 'I'm scared', مون کي **ڪاوڙ آئي** 'I got angry'.
- 'I miss X' = مون کي X **جي ياد** اچي ٿي.
- Scared *of* = **کان** ڊپ; upset *with* = **سان** ناراض.
tip.pattern: مون کي + feeling + لڳي ٿو / اچي ٿي

lessons.title: What do you think?

tip.title: I think that … : ته
tip.body:
- **ته** 'that' links a thought to what you think: مان سمجهان ٿو **ته** … 'I think that …'.
- Also: مون کي لڳي ٿو ته … 'I feel that …', منهنجو خيال آهي ته … 'my view is that …', منهنجي خيال ۾ … 'in my opinion …'.
- After ته comes an ordinary sentence, verb last.
- Ask: تنهنجو / توهان جو **ڇا خيال** آهي؟

tip.title: Agreeing and disagreeing
tip.body:
- Agree: ها، **صحيح** آهي · **بلڪل** · مان **مڃان ٿو** · مان **متفق** آهيان.
- Agree *with* someone = **سان**: مان توهان **سان** متفق آهيان.
- Disagree politely: معاف ڪجو، **پر** … · مان متفق **ناهيان**.

lessons.title: Because, but, so

tip.title: Joining ideas
tip.body:
- **۽** and · **يا** or · **پر** but · **ڇاڪاڻ ته** because · **تنهن ڪري** so · **جيتوڻيڪ** although.
- They start the part they introduce, as in English: مون کي بخار آهي، **تنهن ڪري** گهر ۾ آهيان.
- Hobbies use کي too: مون کي ڪتابن **جو شوق** آهي 'I love books'.
